actions.title: Re-image reference M2316 at the approved BSE settings
evidence: additive-vs-matrix contrast-to-noise 3.2 < 4.0: high-Z phase cannot be segmented reliably (different additive chemistry or beam/detector settings)
actions.rationale: M2316 belongs to the reference, but its additive measurements are not trustworthy at this contrast-to-noise, so those reference statistics rest on one micrograph fewer. Re-imaging restores it; no analysis can.

actions.title: Higher-magnification BSE on reference micrographs: resolve the approved fines below the floor
evidence: the reference high-Z size distribution is highest in its smallest resolved bin (0.36-0.5 µm: 4.95 vs at most 2.90 /1000 µm² above): it has not turned over at the 0.36 µm detection floor, so normal fines below the floor are unobserved
actions.rationale: The reference cannot say what normal looks like below 0.36 µm, so any incoming sub-floor population is compared with an unobserved baseline. A finer pixel (≤ 10 nm) on approved material resolves it.

actions.title: Porosity: space reference fields ≥ 175 µm apart instead of adjacent tiles
evidence: Porosity: adjacent-tile variance 3.6× the short-range prediction (95% CI 2.0-7.8); variogram range ≈ 175 µm
actions.rationale: Adjacent reference tiles re-measure the same structure, so the tile-sampling spread they supply mixes sampling noise with spatial structure. Fields spaced by the correlation range sample it approximately independently.

actions.title: Additive density: one longer coherent reference capture (> 400 µm)
evidence: Additive density: adjacent-tile variance 1.9× the short-range prediction (95% CI 1.1-4.2); variogram still rising at 400 µm (structure larger than the longest coherent capture)
actions.rationale: The variogram has not reached its plateau within the longest reference capture, so the scale of this structure is unknown; one longer mosaic of approved material locates it, and then tells how far apart fields must be.
